title: Shoyu Ramen
subtitle: Japanese soy-seasoned pork broth noodle soup
excerpt: The Tokyo-style ramen: a rich, clear pork and chicken broth seasoned with a soy tare, poured over springy wheat noodles with sliced chashu pork belly, soft-boiled egg, nori, and spring onion. Hours of simmering produce something extraordinary.

recipe.sourceNotes: Ramen is a Japanese noodle soup dish derived from Chinese noodle soups (la mian), introduced to Japan in the late nineteenth century and transformed into something distinctively Japanese. Ramen is classified primarily by its seasoning: shoyu (soy sauce), shio (salt), miso, and tonkotsu (pork bone). Shoyu ramen, associated with Tokyo, uses a clear or lightly coloured pork and chicken broth seasoned with a soy-based tare (concentrated seasoning liquid). The elements are assembled separately and combined in the bowl: the broth, the tare, the noodles (which must be boiled separately and briefly), and the toppings. Chashu pork belly (braised pork belly, rolled and sliced) is the classic topping. Home ramen requires making both the broth and the chashu from scratch; the time investment is significant but the result cannot be replicated any other way.

content.text: Make the chashu pork and the broth a day ahead; both improve overnight and the fat solidifies on the broth for easy removal. The broth should simmer gently, not boil; boiling makes it cloudy. Season each bowl individually with the tare rather than seasoning the whole broth, so each person can adjust to their taste.

content.text: Make the chashu: simmer the rolled pork belly in 500 ml water, the dark soy, 60 ml light soy, sugar, 2 spring onions, and 2 garlic cloves for 2 hours until tender, turning every 30 minutes. Cool in the liquid. Refrigerate overnight; the liquid becomes the tare.

Simmer the chicken stock with the remaining garlic, ginger, and 2 spring onions for 1 hour. Strain and season with salt. Soft-boil the eggs for 7 minutes, then peel and marinate in 50 ml soy sauce diluted with 100 ml water for 1 hour.

To serve: slice the cold chashu into 1 cm rounds. Boil the noodles briefly according to the packet. Heat the broth. Warm the chashu slices. Place noodles in deep bowls. Add 2 tablespoons of the tare (chashu braising liquid) to each bowl. Pour hot broth over. Top with 2 chashu slices, a halved marinated egg, and sliced spring onion.
